run_findings.candidate_010_status: material reader/rotation race remains current; this run verified a platform-specific stable-snapshot implementation rather than one portable handle-pinning strategy
run_findings.candidate_010_posix_snapshot: under shared flock open every selected generation and capture fstat end offsets, release lock, then parse pinned handles only to the captured offsets; local rename witness preserved A/B/C after pathname rotation while unsafe reopen omitted B and reopened C/D
run_findings.candidate_010_end_offset_requirement: a pinned current-file handle sees rows appended after lock release unless parsing is capped at the size captured under the lock; end offsets are required for point-in-time semantics
run_findings.candidate_010_posix_blocking_probe: local synthetic 64MiB JSON scan: hold-shared-lock-through-scan median scan ~0.409s and waiting writer delay ~0.395s; pin+end-offset then release median scan ~0.397s and writer delay ~7.6us; cached local filesystem only, not production performance
run_findings.candidate_010_windows_revision: do not use normal Python pinned handles after releasing the lock on Windows: CPython normal opens do not share delete access, so os.replace/rollover can fail while handles are open; current Argus _maybe_roll swallows rollover exceptions and append then continues, so long pinned scans can silently defer rollover
run_findings.candidate_010_windows_lock_semantics: Microsoft CRT documents _LK_RLCK as the same operation as _LK_LOCK; Argus's existing msvcrt byte-range pattern is therefore suitable as a correctness-first exclusive mutex, not a POSIX-style shared-reader lock
run_findings.candidate_010_windows_adaptation: initial Windows implementation should hold the exclusive cross-platform events.lock through correctness-sensitive scans. A later optimization would need an explicit FILE_SHARE_DELETE opener plus a true shared/exclusive cross-process lock and is higher complexity
run_findings.candidate_010_planner_verdict_fail_close: planner_verdict_was_persisted False authorizes retry emit, so stable-snapshot acquisition/open failure must be an unknown/retry state that leaves the outbox pending and does not re-emit; only a completed stable scan may return False
